name: Four Friends Hide in Silence on a Fire Escape
description: Ahmad, Punchy, Cee, and Ella sit still on a fire escape, pressed close in the shade. The metal grates hum in the heat. Not one of them speaks. They keep their bodies motionless, their voices gone, their eyes low. The air is thick and quiet, broken only by distant street sounds. description: The sun glowed golden orange as it dipped toward the horizon. Around a cardboard box painted with the words WE LOVE, they took turns showing off new moves—spins, hops, sharp arm gestures—each trying something different. Laughter broke out as one stumbled, then quickly joined back in. They danced together, then apart, adjusting steps, repeating sequences, testing names under their breath.

description: Pino pulls Vito aside and speaks to him urgently, telling him not to trust Mookie. Da Mayor keeps asking, 'What makes Sammy run?' even after Eddie repeats his name. Eventually, Da Mayor tells Eddie to relax and asks how much he would want to run an errand to the corner store. Eddie asks what he’s supposed to buy, and Da Mayor says he wants a quart of Budweiser, to be picked up for his father. They settle on fifty cents. He looks at them and asks what they know about him, saying they can’t even pee straight. He tells them they don’t know his pain, that they’ve never stood in a doorway hearing their five children go hungry with nothing they could do. He tells them not to call him a bum or a drunk, that it’s disrespectful, and that their parents raised them better. The teenagers fall silent. Ella says, 'He told you off.' Vito looks surprised and asks who told her, insisting that Pino doesn’t push him around and that he holds his own. He asks again if Mookie said something. Jade tells him to forget it, to forget she brought it up. Vito continues to defend himself, but Jade doesn’t respond, ending the conversation.
related_events: Jade questions Vito about Pino's treatment of him
Vito defends himself against Jade's implication about Pino
Jade withdraws her question about Pino and Vito
related_occasions: Jade'S Visit To Sal'S Famous Pizzeria

name: Officers Ponte and Long Confront the Corner Men
description: Officers Ponte and Long drive down the block and come to a stop at the corner. They sit in their patrol car, staring at Sweet Dick Willie, ML, and Coconut Sid, who stand on the corner and return their gaze without speaking. After a moment of silence, the officers pull away and drive off. The Corner Men remain on the corner, watching the car disappear down the street.
related_events: Police car stops at corner and officers glare at Corner Men
Officers Ponte and Long drive away from the corner

name: ML Points Out the Korean Market
description: After the police car drives away, ML turns his attention to the Korean fruit and vegetable stand across the street. He points it out to Sweet Dick Willie and Coconut Sid, who are sitting with him on the corner. 'Look at that,' ML says. 'It's a fucking shame.' Sweet Dick Willie asks what he means. ML tells them to listen closely, then says, 'Look at those Korean motherfuckers across the street. I betcha they haven't been a year off da motherfucking boat before they opened up their own place.' Coconut Sid adds that it's been about a year. ML continues, noting how quickly the Koreans opened a successful business in a building that had been boarded up for years. He says he can't figure it out—either Koreans are geniuses or Black people are dumb. The three men fall silent. Coconut Sid says it must be because they're Black, and nobody wants Black people to succeed. Sweet Dick Willie calls it an old excuse. ML says he'd be happy to see a Black-owned business open there and would be the first to spend his money. Sweet Dick Willie gets up, saying it's Miller time, and walks off toward the market. ML shakes his head and says it's a motherfucking shame. Coconut Sid agrees.
related_events: ML points out Korean fruit and vegetable stand across the street
ML explains something important to Sweet Dick Willie and Coconut Sid

name: ML, Sweet Dick Willie, and Coconut Sid Discuss the Korean Market
description: ML points across the street at the Korean fruit and vegetable stand, shaking his head. He says the owners must have come off the boat no more than a year ago and already have a thriving business in a building that had been boarded up for years. Coconut Sid notes it has been about a year since they opened. Sweet Dick Willie stays quiet at first, then mutters that ML wasn’t saying anything before the cops interrupted. ML insists it’s a shame how quickly the Koreans set up shop while Black folks don’t have businesses like that in the neighborhood. He wonders aloud if it’s because Koreans are geniuses or Black people are dumb. The three men fall silent, staring across the street. Coconut Sid finally says it must be because they’re Black—nobody wants Black people to succeed. Sweet Dick Willie calls it an old excuse. ML says he’d be the first to support a Black-owned business if one opened here. Sweet Dick Willie gets up, says it’s Miller time, and walks toward the Korean stand. ML and Coconut Sid watch him go, then look back at the market. ML mutters it’s a damn shame. Coconut Sid agrees.
related_events: ML expresses resentment toward Korean business owners across the street
Sweet Dick Willie and Coconut Sid respond to ML's commentary on racial economic disparity
The group reflects silently on the question of racial inequality in business ownership

name: Sweet Dick Willie Buys Beer from the Korean Stand
description: Sweet Dick Willie gets up from his folding chair and walks across the street to the Korean fruit and vegetable stand. He buys a beer, opening it as he stands near the corner. The other men watch in silence as he takes a drink.
related_events: Sweet Dick Willie decides to buy beer from the Korean stand

name: Officers Finish Meal and Leave the Pizzeria
description: Sal took the food out of the oven, wrapped it up, and handed it to Officers Ponte and Long. Officer Ponte paid nine-fifty for the meal. The officers said their goodbyes, with Officer Long calling out to Vito and Pino, then left the pizzeria. As they walked out, Mookie came in.
related_events: Sal removes food from oven and hands it to officers
Officer Ponte pays for food at pizzeria
Officers Ponte and Long leave pizzeria after meal

name: Mookie Arrives and Clashes with Sal Over Delivery Complaints
description: Mookie walks into the pizzeria just as Officers Ponte and Long head out. He immediately starts complaining that he can't run faster with pizzas without the cheese sliding to one side, saying Sal would need to give him a jet rocket if he wanted quicker deliveries. Sal smirks and tells him he must have a guilty conscience since he came in so defensive. Mookie insists he hasn't done anything wrong. Sal keeps needling him, asking what he could possibly be guilty of, then laughs at his own joke. As Sal turns away, Pino pulls Vito toward the back room.
related_events: Mookie enters pizzeria as officers depart
Mookie complains about pizza delivery speed limitations
Sal teases Mookie about having a guilty conscience
Mookie denies being guilty of anything
Sal implies Mookie's guilt through continued teasing

name: Pino pulls Vito into the back
description: Sal laughs at his own joke as the banter with Mookie continues in the front of the pizzeria. While Sal is distracted, Pino takes hold of Vito and pulls him away from the scene, leading him toward the back of the restaurant.
related_events: Sal laughs at his own joke while redirecting conversation
Pino pulls Vito into the back of the pizzeria

name: Da Mayor Brings Flowers to Mother Sister
description: Da Mayor walks up to Mother Sister's brownstone holding a bouquet of fresh-cut flowers arranged in a repurposed wine bottle. He extends the flowers toward her as she sits in her window, but she does not acknowledge him. He takes a seat on the steps, brings the flowers to his face, and remarks on their scent, asking if she agrees. She remains silent. He sets the bouquet down and observes that the summer heat makes the smell of garbage stronger, overpowering the fragrance of the blooms. The sun begins to set, and he expresses quiet gratitude, speaking of the coming cool breeze. He says he will rest a moment and then be on his way. He looks up at the sky as the light shifts, the air still and quiet around him.
related_events: Da Mayor approaches Mother Sister's brownstone with flowers
Mother Sister ignores Da Mayor's gesture of offering flowers
Da Mayor sits on the steps and comments on the flower scent
Da Mayor reflects on summer heat intensifying garbage odor

name: Da Mayor Sits on the Stoop at Dusk
description: Da Mayor remains seated on the steps of the brownstone, the repurposed wine bottle with flowers resting beside him. The sun sinks low, casting orange and purple streaks across the sky. He lifts his face toward the light, breathing in the evening air, and murmurs words of thanks. He speaks of the cooling breeze that may come, and mentions Jesus in a soft, steady voice. After a pause, he says he will rest a moment and then be on his way. He does not look at Mother Sister. His eyes stay on the sky, still and quiet, as the light fades around him.
related_events: Da Mayor expresses gratitude as the sun begins to set
Da Mayor invokes Jesus with warm and patient tone
Da Mayor gazes upward without pressing for response

name: Da Mayor Sits on the Stoop as the Sun Sets
description: Da Mayor sits on the steps of Mother Sister's brownstone, the bouquet of flowers resting beside him. He looks up at the sky as the sun sinks below the horizon, its light spreading in vivid streaks of orange and purple. The colors deepen across the sky, casting a quiet glow over the street.
related_events: camera captures close-up of vividly colored setting sun

name: Radio Raheem Enters Sal's with Blaring Music and Orders Pizza
description: Radio Raheem walks into Sal's pizzeria with music loudly playing from his boombox. He stands calmly and says, 'Two slices.' Sal refuses to serve him until the music is turned off. Pino echoes the demand, telling Radio Raheem to shut it down. The tension rises as Sal, Vito, Pino, and customers watch closely. Sal reaches under the counter and pulls out his Mickey Mantle bat, holding it in plain sight. Radio Raheem looks around, smiles, and turns the music off. He repeats his order: 'Two slices, extra cheese.' Sal slides the bat back under the counter and says the extra cheese will cost two dollars. He adds that no music is allowed in his pizzeria, especially no rap, and asks if Radio Raheem understands.
related_events: Radio Raheem enters Sal's pizzeria with music blaring
Radio Raheem demands two slices of pizza
Sal refuses service until music is turned off
Pino demands Radio Raheem turn off the music

name: Sal Retrieves Bat, Standoff at Pizzeria
description: Radio Raheem enters Sal's Famous Pizzeria with music blaring. He asks for two slices. Sal demands he turn off the music, saying there’s no service while it’s playing. Pino tells Radio Raheem to turn it off. Sal complains he can’t think and that the music is disturbing him and his customers. Sal reaches under the counter and pulls out his Mickey Mantle baseball bat. Everyone in the pizzeria—Sal, Radio Raheem, Vito, Pino, and the customers—stands still, watching. The music stops. Radio Raheem says he wants two slices with extra cheese. Sal puts the bat back under the counter. He tells Radio Raheem that no music is allowed in his place of business and that extra cheese costs two dollars.
related_events: Sal retrieves Mickey Mantle bat from under the counter

name: Radio Raheem Turns Off the Music and Orders Pizza
description: Radio Raheem smiles, turns off his boombox, and calmly asks for two slices of pizza with extra cheese. Sal places his bat back under the counter, states that no music is allowed in the pizzeria, and tells Radio Raheem the extra cheese will cost two dollars.
related_events: Radio Raheem turns off the boombox and requests pizza with extra cheese
Sal reiterates pizzeria rule against music and quotes price for extra cheese

name: Jade and Mookie Meet Buggin' Out at the Fire Hydrant
description: Buggin' Out stands on a fire hydrant, one foot propped up as he tries to clean a dirty Air Jordan. Jade and Mookie walk up to him. Buggin' Out remarks that it's nice to see a family spending time together. Mookie replies that they're not hanging out—he's being escorted back to work. Jade corrects him, saying she just wants a slice of pizza. Buggin' Out tells Jade he's organizing a boycott of Sal's Famous Pizzeria. He points out that all the photos on the Wall of Fame inside the pizzeria are of Italian people. Jade asks if he's spoken to Sal about it. Buggin' Out says he has, and explains that he doesn't want anyone from the community spending money at Sal's until Black faces are added to the wall. Jade looks at him skeptically and suggests he could use his energy in a more useful way. Buggin' Out interprets this as her not supporting the cause. Jade says she is down, but only for worthwhile causes. They exchange affirmations of love before Mookie leaves and Jade prepares to follow.
related_events: Buggin' Out attempts to clean his soiled Air Jordan while standing on a fire hydrant
Jade and Mookie approach Buggin' Out
related_occasions: Planned Boycott Of Sal'S Famous Pizzeria

name: Buggin' Out Announces Boycott of Sal's Pizzeria
description: Buggin' Out stands with one foot on a fire hydrant, cleaning his soiled Air Jordan, when Jade and Mookie approach. He comments on the sight of them together, calling it nice to see a family hanging out. Mookie clarifies he is being escorted back to work, but Jade corrects him, saying she just wants a slice of pizza. Buggin' Out tells Jade he is organizing a boycott of Sal's Famous Pizzeria. When she asks what Sal did, Buggin' Out points out that all the photos on the Wall of Fame are of Italian people. He says he wants Black faces on the wall and demands that no one from the community spend money at Sal's until the change is made. Jade looks at him skeptically and suggests he could use his energy more productively. Buggin' Out interprets her response as disapproval, and she confirms she is not supporting the boycott, though she says she still loves him. He replies that he still loves her too. Mookie, having stayed only briefly, leaves before the conversation ends.

Buggin' Out demands Black representation on the Wall Of Fame

description: Buggin' Out stands with one foot on a fire hydrant, cleaning his soiled Air Jordan, when Jade and Mookie approach. He says no one from the community should spend money there until Black faces are added to the wall. Jade looks at him skeptically and suggests he could direct his energy toward more worthwhile causes. Buggin’ Out acknowledges she’s not on board, but says he still loves her. Mookie departs from the conversation

name: Buggin' Out and Jade Disagree on the Boycott but Affirm Their Bond
description: Buggin' Out stands with one foot on a fire hydrant, cleaning his soiled Air Jordan, when Jade and Mookie approach. Buggin' Out comments on how nice it looks to see a family together, but Mookie clarifies he’s being escorted back to work, and Jade adds she just wants a slice of pizza. Buggin' Out acknowledges she isn’t on board. She says she’s down, but only for worthwhile causes. Before parting, Buggin' Out says, 'Jade, I still love you.' Jade replies, 'I still love you too.'

Jade reciprocates affection while withholding support

name: Buggin' Out Confronts Clifton Over Damaged Sneakers
description: Buggin' Out is walking down the block when Clifton accidentally bumps into him, stepping on his new white Air Jordans. A dark smudge marks the pristine shoe. Buggin' Out looks at his sneakers, then chases Clifton down the street. He demands an apology, pointing out that Clifton not only knocked into him but also ruined his newly bought shoes. Clifton turns, apologizes, and says he’s sorry. Buggin' Out argues that a simple 'excuse me' isn’t enough, especially after stepping on his fresh Jordans. A crowd gathers, including Ahmad, Cee, Punchy, and Ella. They observe the shoes and comment on the damage, noting how much the sneakers cost and how bad they now look. Buggin' Out accuses Clifton of disrespect, questions why he’s living in the neighborhood, and denounces gentrification. Clifton replies that he owns a brownstone on the block. Buggin' Out challenges his right to buy property there. The crowd reacts, laughing and encouraging Buggin' Out. When Clifton says he has the right to live where he wants, Buggin' Out grows angrier, calling the idea of a free country ridiculous. He threatens to attack but claims he won’t because he’s a righteous Black man. He tells Clifton to cross the street next time they meet and demands he buy a new pair of sneakers. Clifton says he’s leaving and walks away. Buggin' Out tells him to move back to Connecticut as the crowd watches on.
related_events: Clifton accidentally bumps into Buggin' Out and steps on his new sneakers
Buggin' Out confronts Clifton about the sneaker incident

name: Buggin' Out Confronts Clifton Over Sneakers and Gentrification
description: Buggin' Out confronts Clifton after Clifton steps on his new white Air Jordans, leaving a black smudge on the shoe. Buggin' Out demands an apology, pointing out that Clifton not only bumped into him but also failed to show proper respect. Clifton turns around, apologizes, and says he is sorry. Buggin' Out argues that the incident is not just about the shoes, but about Clifton being on his side of the block and living in the neighborhood. He questions who gave Clifton the right to be there, accusing him of contributing to gentrification. Clifton responds that he owns a brownstone on the block and believes he has the right to live where he chooses. Buggin' Out challenges the idea, asking who allowed Clifton to buy property in the neighborhood. A crowd forms, including Ahmad, Cee, Punchy, and Ella, who react with laughter and encouragement as the argument intensifies. Ahmad comments that the sneakers are ruined, and Cee adds that they might as well be thrown out. Punchy notes they looked good before the incident, and Ella remarks that Buggin' Out used to be so fine. Ahmad asks how much the shoes cost, and Cee says a hundred dollars. Buggin' Out tells Clifton he should buy him a new pair, then warns him that if he were not a righteous Black man, Clifton would be in serious trouble. The crowd shows approval. Buggin' Out tells Clifton to move back to Connecticut and to cross the street the next time he sees him coming.
related_events: Buggin' Out escalates the confrontation with accusations of gentrification
Clifton apologizes but defends his right to live in the neighborhood
Crowd gathers and reacts to the escalating argument

name: Buggin' Out Demands New Jordans and Tells Clifton to Leave
description: Buggin' Out glares at his sneakers, now marked with a dark scuff from Clifton's foot. He turns to Clifton, voice rising. "You should buy me another pair." The crowd watches closely. Ahmad points at the shoes. "Your Jordans are dogged." Cee adds, "You might as well throw 'em out." Punchy shakes his head. "They looked good before he messed them up." Ella sighs. "You used to be so fine." Ahmad turns to Buggin' Out. "How much did you pay for them?" Cee answers, "A hundred bucks." Ahmad whistles. "A hundred bucks!" Buggin' Out steps forward. "You're lucky the Black man has a loving heart. Next time you see me coming, cross the street quick." Ahmad nods. "He's dissing you." Buggin' Out continues, "If I wasn't a righteous Black man, you'd be in serious trouble. SERIOUS." The crowd murmurs in agreement. Clifton takes a step back. "I'm gonna leave now." Buggin' Out shouts after him, "Move back to Connecticut!"
related_events: Buggin' Out demands Clifton buy him a new pair of Jordans
Buggin' Out threatens Clifton after sneaker damage
Ahmad and Cee mock the condition of Buggin' Out's damaged Jordans
Buggin' Out tells Clifton to move back to Connecticut

name: Clifton Leaves the Confrontation
description: Clifton says he is going to leave and turns to walk away. The crowd watches as he steps back, ending the encounter.
related_events: Clifton attempts to disengage and leave the confrontation

name: Tina Takes the Pizza, Mookie Initiates a Kiss
description: Tina watches Mookie as he stands before her. She reaches out, takes the pizza from his hands, and sets it on the floor. Mookie moves toward her, grabs her, and begins to kiss her.
related_events: Tina takes pizza from Mookie's hands and places it on the floor
Mookie begins kissing Tina after she takes the pizza

name: Tina Confronts Mookie About the Forgotten Ice Cream
description: Tina sees that Mookie hasn’t brought the Hagen-Dazs butter pecan ice cream she wanted. She tells him his memory is getting bad. Mookie says he just forgot. Tina says she really wanted it. Mookie offers to go out and get it. Tina quickly refuses, saying he won’t come back if he leaves. Mookie says he can’t stay long. Tina asks how long he can stay. Mookie says long enough to have sex. Tina refuses, saying it’s too hot and she won’t let him get what he wants and then leave without seeing him again for days. Mookie suggests a quick encounter. Tina calls him a fool. Mookie says they can do something else instead. Tina asks what else. Mookie tells her to trust him. Tina repeats that she should trust him, pointing out that trusting him is how they ended up with a son. Mookie tells her to trust him again and pushes her back into her bedroom.
related_events: Tina confronts Mookie about forgetting to bring ice cream
Mookie offers to go get the ice cream after forgetting it
Tina refuses Mookie's offer to get ice cream, fearing he won't return

name: Tina Confronts Mookie About Trust
description: Mookie suggests they have a quick sexual encounter, but Tina refuses, saying it’s too hot and that she doesn’t want him to get dressed and leave, disappearing for days as he has before. Mookie says they can do something else instead. Tina looks at him skeptically and asks what he means, questioning his reliability. When Mookie tells her to trust him, she responds by reminding him that because she trusted him, they have a son. Mookie doesn’t answer but pushes her back into the bedroom.
related_events: Mookie suggests having a quick sexual encounter with Tina
Tina refuses Mookie's suggestion due to fear of abandonment
Mookie proposes an alternative activity instead of sex
Tina challenges Mookie's reliability by referencing their son

name: Mookie Pushes Tina Into the Bedroom
description: After Tina questions Mookie about trust and bringing up their son, Mookie pushes her back into her bedroom.
related_events: Mookie pushes Tina back into her bedroom

name: Radio Raheem Turns Up the Volume
description: Radio Raheem stands in front of the stoop and cranks up the volume on his boombox as salsa music blares from a nearby parked car. The sound of his rap music grows louder, clashing with the salsa until both fill the air in a roaring competition. The men on the stoop stop their game, look over, and begin shouting at him in Spanish. The noise from both radios continues to surge, each trying to overpower the other.
related_events: Radio Raheem increases volume to overpower competing salsa music
Rap and salsa music clash in a deafening auditory standoff

name: Puerto Rican Men Confront Radio Raheem
description: The group of Puerto Rican men on the stoop notice Radio Raheem turning up his boombox, the rap music growing louder over the salsa playing from their parked car. They look at him and begin shouting in Spanish, their voices rising in protest. Stevie gets up, walks to the car, and turns the salsa music off. Radio Raheem smiles, nods, and lowers the volume of his boombox before walking down the block. Once he is gone, Stevie turns the salsa music back on. The men mutter in Spanish, shaking their heads.
related_events: Puerto Rican men confront Radio Raheem in Spanish
Stevie turns off the car radio to reduce competing music

name: Stevie Turns Off the Car Radio
description: Stevie gets up from the stoop, walks to the parked car, and turns off the radio. The salsa music stops. Radio Raheem stands in front of the stoop, smiles, nods, and turns his boombox down to a lower volume. He begins walking down the block. The men on the stoop mutter in Spanish and shake their heads. Stevie turns the car radio back on.
related_events: Radio Raheem lowers boombox volume in response to reduced competition
Stevie turns off the car radio to reduce competing music

name: Stevie Turns the Salsa Back On
description: After Radio Raheem smiles, turns his boombox down, and walks away, Stevie returns to the parked car. He reaches inside and turns the salsa music back on. The men on the stoop mutter in Spanish, shaking their heads as the music fills the air once more.
related_events: Stevie restarts salsa music after Radio Raheem's adjustment
Puerto Rican men express frustration in Spanish at ongoing music conflict

name: Stevie Acknowledges Radio Raheem's Sound
description: Stevie gets up from the stoop, walks to the car, and turns off the salsa music. Radio Raheem stands in front of the group, his boombox blasting rap music. He smiles, nods, and lowers the volume slightly before walking down the block. Stevie says, 'You got it, bro.' The other men on the stoop mutter in Spanish, shaking their heads. Stevie turns the salsa music back on.
related_events: Stevie acknowledges Radio Raheem's musical dominance verbally
Radio Raheem resumes dominant position with adjusted volume

name: Ice Cream Vendor Serves Flavored Ices to Children
description: An old Puerto Rican man pushes a cart labeled HELADO DE COCO down the street. A block of ice sits atop the cart, surrounded by bottles of colored syrup. He scrapes shavings from the ice into a paper cup and pours syrup over them. A group of children waits eagerly, and he hands one of them the finished treat.
related_events: Ice cream vendor scrapes ice and serves flavored ices to children

name: Eddie Chases the Mister Softee Truck
description: The familiar tune of the Mister Softee truck echoes down the street as it approaches. Eddie Lovell, a young boy playing on the sidewalk, looks up and jumps to his feet. He sprints into the street, chasing the moving ice cream truck. The sound of the music grows louder as the truck continues forward, drawing Eddie's full attention.
related_events: Mister Softee truck approaches playing children

name: Eddie Chases the Mister Softee Truck into Traffic
description: Eddie Lovell, a young boy playing on the sidewalk, hears the familiar tune of the Mister Softee truck approaching. He jumps up and runs into the street, chasing the ice cream truck without looking. A speeding car comes into view, heading straight toward him.
related_events: Eddie Lovell runs into the street chasing the Mister Softee truck

name: Da Mayor Saves Eddie from a Speeding Car
description: Da Mayor sees a speeding car heading toward Eddie, who is running into the street after the Mister Softee truck. He sprints across the road, knocks Eddie down to save him, and both are struck by the car. They fall to the ground, shaken and hurt. Eddie begins to cry, and Da Mayor picks him up, telling him not to cry and that he’s safe. A crowd gathers around them as Eddie’s mother, Louise, pushes through and hugs her son. When Eddie says Da Mayor knocked him down, Louise scolds Da Mayor, but he explains that he was saving the boy from being hit. The crowd confirms his account. Louise asks Eddie if it’s true, but he stays silent. She hits him, scolding him for lying and playing in the street, then orders him upstairs. She warns that his father will punish him too when he comes home. Da Mayor tells her the boy didn’t need to be hit, as he was already frightened. Louise thanks him for helping but says no one will tell her how to raise her child. Da Mayor nods and tips his hat as she leaves.
related_events: Da Mayor rescues Eddie from oncoming speeding car
Da Mayor comforts injured and crying Eddie after rescue
Crowd gathers at accident scene after rescue

name: Louise Confronts Da Mayor After Eddie's Rescue
description: Louise, Eddie's mother, pushes through the crowd and rushes to her son, who is crying in Da Mayor's arms. She asks what is wrong. Eddie says, "Mayor knocked me down." Louise turns to Da Mayor and scolds him, saying he should be ashamed. Da Mayor explains that he saw the car speeding toward Eddie, ran into the street, and knocked the boy out of the way to save his life. The crowd confirms his account. Louise then turns to Eddie and demands to know if it is true. Eddie stays silent. She repeats her question, but he does not answer. Da Mayor says the boy is fine, just scared. Louise strikes Eddie on the buttocks, telling him not to lie and not to play in the street. She hits him repeatedly as he cries, "Mommy! Mommy! I'm sorry." After each strike, she repeats her reprimands. Eddie runs off when she tells him to go upstairs. Louise warns that his father will punish him too when he comes home. Da Mayor says she didn't need to hit the boy, as he was already frightened. Louise thanks him for saving Eddie but says no one, not even the boy's father, will tell her how to raise her child. Da Mayor acknowledges her right. Louise leaves, and he tips his hat as she walks away.
related_events: Louise confronts Da Mayor about Eddie's condition after rescue
Da Mayor explains his actions during the rescue to Louise
Louise questions Eddie about the truth of the incident
Louise physically disciplines Eddie for lying and playing in the street
Eddie runs away after being disciplined by Louise
Louise asserts authority over Eddie's upbringing to Da Mayor

name: Da Mayor Tips His Hat After Confrontation with Louise
description: After Louise scolds Eddie and sends him upstairs, Da Mayor tells her he didn’t think she needed to hit the boy, saying he was already scared. Louise thanks him for helping her son but says no one, not even the boy’s father, has the right to question how she raises him. Da Mayor replies that she’s right. Louise walks away, and Da Mayor tips his hat to her as she leaves.
related_events: Da Mayor tips his hat to Louise after confrontation

name: Mother Sister Calls Out to Da Mayor After His Brave Act
description: Mother Sister calls to Da Mayor from her window as he walks by. He stops and looks at her, a smile appearing on his face. She tells him that what he did was foolish but brave, and that the child owes him his life. Da Mayor replies that he wasn’t trying to be a hero—he simply reacted without thinking. He adds that he hasn’t run that fast in years. Mother Sister tells him she wanted to thank him for doing a good thing. Da Mayor thanks her in return. She says he’s welcome, and he tips his hat before moving on.
related_events: Mother Sister calls out to Da Mayor from her window
Da Mayor stops and smiles upon being addressed by Mother Sister
Mother Sister acknowledges Da Mayor's brave act of saving a child

name: Da Mayor's Instinctive Rescue and Reflection
description: Da Mayor walks past Mother Sister's window when she calls out to him, acknowledging what he did. He stops and smiles, looking up at her. She tells him his act was foolish but brave, and that the boy owes him his life. Da Mayor replies that he wasn't trying to be a hero—he saw what was about to happen and reacted without thinking. He says if he had taken time to consider, he might not have acted at all. He adds that he’s an old man and hasn’t run that fast in years. Then, he recalls a moment from his youth—scoring the winning run on a bunt single in a baseball game on August 1, 1939, in Snow Hill, Alabama. Mother Sister tells him maybe he shouldn’t try being heroic again, that this changes nothing between them, but that she wanted to thank him. Da Mayor thanks her in return. He tips his hat, and stands there quietly.
related_events: Da Mayor explains he acted instinctively to prevent harm
Da Mayor reflects on his physical effort despite his age

name: Da Mayor Recalls a Baseball Triumph and Ponders Heroism
description: Da Mayor stops walking and looks at Mother Sister as she speaks to him from her window. He smiles, then recalls a moment from 1939, when he ran from first to home on a bunt single, scoring the winning run in a baseball game in Snow Hill, Alabama. Warming to the memory, he says he hasn’t run that fast in years and muses that he might consider being heroic more often. Mother Sister replies that perhaps he shouldn’t, telling him not to get happy, that this changes nothing between them. She adds that he did a good thing and she wanted to thank him. Da Mayor nods and says he thanks her. She says he’s welcome. He tips his hat and stands quietly before her.
